Yeah just finished deep research. All 4 detection fixes are built and compiling. Here's what else can be done to improve detection, ranked by impact vs effort:

Tier 1 — High impact, can do now:

Spectral flux onset detection — run a tiny parallel pipeline using vDSP FFT that detects sudden energy spikes (knocks, claps, glass) in <100ms. When a spike is detected, boost the Apple classifier's confidence for the next few frames. Costs almost nothing computationally — just math on the audio buffer you already have. This is the single biggest win for transient sounds.

Replace median filter with per-class post-processing — right now every sound gets the same 3-frame median filter which kills transient spikes. Instead: transient sounds (knock, clap, glass) get peak-hold smoothing (fast attack, slow decay — preserves the spike), sustained sounds (siren, baby cry) keep the median filter. One code change, huge improvement for transients.

Train a CreateML custom sound classifier — Apple has MLSoundClassifier in CreateML. You record actual phone mic audio of knocks, claps, doorbells etc. in real rooms. It uses Apple's Audio Feature Print as the backbone (same pipeline as SoundAnalysis) but fine-tuned to YOUR audio conditions. Produces a .mlmodel that drops right into SNClassifySoundRequest. This solves the core problem — Apple's model was trained on YouTube audio, not phone mics.

Tier 2 — Medium effort, strong payoff:

Fine-tune EfficientAT on phone audio — you already have the model pipeline. The issue isn't the architecture, it's domain gap (YouTube vs phone mic). Fine-tune mn05_as (tiny variant, <0.25s inference) on FSD50K dataset + phone-recorded samples with noise augmentation. Then use it as a consensus second opinion alongside Apple.

Adaptive gain control — normalize audio levels dynamically so a distant knock gets boosted to the same level as a nearby clap. Simple running RMS computation → apply gain. Helps with "it works when I'm close but not from across the room."

RNNoise preprocessing — open-source hybrid DSP/neural noise suppressor (10ms latency, runs on CPU). Clean the audio before classification. Removes AC hum, fan noise, etc. that confuse the classifier.

Tier 3 — Bigger lift, cutting edge:

FAST model (Jan 2025) — 150x fewer parameters than Audio Spectrogram Transformer, matches accuracy. Designed for on-device. Would need CoreML conversion using convmelspec (Adobe's tool that converts mel spectrograms to CoreML-compatible 1D convolutions). Best new architecture out there for this use case.

tinyCLAP — 6% of CLAP's parameters, enables zero-shot sound classification using text descriptions ("a door knock", "glass breaking"). Add new sound types without collecting training data. Wild but real.

Whisper encoder repurposed — WhisperKit already runs Whisper on iOS via CoreML with ANE acceleration. Here's the full breakdown of differences between **tapticoriginal** and **tapticios** sound detection:

---

## Core Architecture

| Aspect | tapticoriginal | tapticios |
|--------|---|---|
| **SystemAudioClassifier** | 561 lines, simple linear pipeline | 1585 lines (+182%), multi-layered |
| **Audio Window** | Fixed 1.5s | Dual window: 0.5s (transients) + 3.0s (sustained) |
| **Global Threshold** | Hardcoded 0.75 for all sounds | 40+ per-sound profiles (0.22–0.50) |
| **Pre-filtering** | None | 4-stage: OOD detection, entropy rejection, gap check, confusable pair suppression |
| **Post-processing** | None | Per-sound median filter |
| **Background Reliability** | Fire-and-forget | Health checks every 30s, auto-recovery after 3 failures, background task renewal |
| **Learning** | None | AdaptiveThresholdManager learns from user feedback |
| **Debounce** | Fixed 1.5s | Per-sound: 0.5s (transient) to 1.5s (sustained) |
| **Noise Gate** | None | Adaptive RMS-based gate for early rejection |
| **Sound Catalog** | Raw Apple label strings | 119 curated sounds with severity, icons, focus groups |
| **GPU Control** | Default | Explicit CPU-only mode |
| **Custom Models** | None | EfficientATModel.mlpackage + DomesticSoundClassifier.mlmodel available |

## Key New Systems in tapticios

1. **ClassificationPreFilter** — Rejects garbage frames before per-sound processing (OOD detection, ambiguity rejection, confusable pair suppression)
2. **SoundDetectionConfig** — Every sound has its own threshold, measurement count, window duration, and category
3. **AdaptiveThresholdManager** — Thresholds shift based on user false-positive/confirmed reports (+0.02 per FP, -0.005 per confirm)
4. **Dual-window inference** — Short window catches knocks/claps fast, long window catches sirens/alarms accurately
5. **Health monitoring** — Background timer + GCD checks, audio route change handling, auto-restart on failure
6. **SoundCatalog** — 119 sounds organized by severity, browse category, and focus groups

## Concrete Example: Doorbell Detection

**Original**: Audio → is confidence > 0.75? → wait 1.5s debounce → detect

**Current**: Audio → noise gate → dual window (0.5s preferred) → OOD check → ambiguity check → confusable pair check (bell/doorbell/phone_bell) → per-sound threshold 0.35 → adaptive adjustment from user feedback → median filter → 3 consecutive measurements → 0.5s debounce → detect

---
